$comment: Single source of truth for the twelve collections. Read by the website (src/lib/catalog.ts) and the brand asset generator (scripts/brand). Formats, strengths and flavour profiles follow the Heritage Cigars reference sheet (October 2026) and are proposals until each blend is confirmed with its manufacturer: keep specStatus 'concept' and leave wrapper, binder, filler, country and manufacturer null until verified.

collections.name: Caesar
collections.inspiration: The order, architecture and laurel-crowned authority of imperial Rome.
collections.story: Rome measured its power in roads, aqueducts and law as much as in conquest. The laurel wreath, awarded to victorious generals and later worn by emperors, became the shorthand for that authority. The Caesar collection borrows Rome's discipline: a crimson field, a closed laurel and the four letters that stood on every standard — SPQR, the Senate and People of Rome.

emblem.note: SPQR was the formal signature of the Roman state; used here as a historical inscription, not a modern civic mark.

products.name: Caesar Robusto
products.summary: A classic robusto: the compact, full-flavoured anchor of the Roman collection.
products.description: The Caesar Robusto is a short, generous-gauge parejo that delivers its character in under an hour. Format, strength and flavour profile follow the Heritage Cigars reference sheet; the blend will be developed with a Latin American partner manufacturer.

collections.name: Pharaoh
collections.inspiration: Geometry, permanence and the lapis-blue luxury of the Nile kingdoms.
collections.story: For three thousand years Egypt's rulers built to outlast them. Pyramids aligned to the compass, temples set against the sun, lapis lazuli carried from distant mountains to colour royal ornament. The Pharaoh collection takes its order from that geometry: a lapis field and a single disc rising over a stepped monument.

emblem.note: Architectural motif; avoids deity imagery and hieroglyphic text.

products.name: Pharaoh Toro
products.summary: A balanced toro with a long, even draw.
products.description: A six-inch toro with a 52 ring gauge: enough length to develop and enough girth to stay cool. Spice, cedar and honey are the profile the blend is being developed toward.

collections.name: Tsar
collections.inspiration: Winter palaces, court ceremony and the jewelled crowns of St Petersburg.
collections.story: From Peter the Great's new capital on the Neva to the court ceremonies of the nineteenth century, the Russian Empire staged its power with extraordinary craft — goldsmiths, enamellers and jewellers working at the scale of an empire. The Tsar collection is the long, slow format of the range: an oxblood field and a domed crown drawn in gold.

emblem.note: A generic domed-crown silhouette; deliberately avoids state heraldry such as the double-headed eagle.

products.name: Tsar Churchill
products.summary: A long, stately churchill for unhurried evenings.
products.description: A seven-inch churchill built for a long smoke, with the fullest profile in the range alongside Napoleon, Genghis and Imperator.

collections.name: Suleiman
collections.inspiration: The tulip, the tile and the refinement of the Ottoman court at its height.
collections.story: Suleiman I's reign is remembered as a high point of Ottoman law, architecture and the arts — the age of the architect Sinan and of the tulip and carnation designs that spread across Iznik tiles, textiles and manuscripts. The Suleiman collection takes the tulip as its sign, drawn in gold on a deep Ottoman green.

emblem.note: The tulip is a decorative Ottoman motif; religious symbols and the imperial tughra are deliberately not used.

products.name: Suleiman Torpedo
products.summary: A torpedo whose pointed head concentrates the draw.
products.description: A six-inch figurado tapering to a point at the head. The shape echoes the tulip of the Ottoman emblem; the blend is aimed at spice, floral notes and leather.

collections.name: Akbar
collections.inspiration: Cusped arches, carved stone screens and the jade and ivory of Mughal craft.
collections.story: Akbar built an empire across northern India and a court known for its patronage of painting, architecture and debate. Mughal builders framed their spaces with cusped arches and pierced stone screens; their craftsmen carved jade with remarkable delicacy. The Akbar collection is the lightest of the range, framed by a single arch in pale jade and gold.

emblem.note: Architectural motif drawn from Mughal arches and jali screens.

products.name: Akbar Corona Gorda
products.summary: A smooth corona gorda with refined proportions.
products.description: A slightly fuller corona, chosen for balance rather than power: nutty, floral and smooth.

collections.name: Napoleon
collections.inspiration: Neoclassical order, imperial blue and the golden bee of the First Empire.
collections.story: When Napoleon crowned himself emperor in 1804 he chose the bee as an emblem, linking his new dynasty to the ancient Frankish king Childeric, in whose tomb golden bee-shaped ornaments had been found. The Napoleon collection carries that bee in gold on a deep imperial blue — compact, decisive and precise.

emblem.note: The Napoleonic bee is a historical emblem; no modern state insignia are used.

products.name: Napoleon Double Corona
products.summary: A grand double corona with a full, rich profile.
products.description: At seven and a half inches, the Napoleon Double Corona is one of the two longest parejos in the range, built for coffee, cocoa and caramel at full strength.

collections.name: Cyrus
collections.period: Founded by Cyrus the Great, c. 550 BC
collections.inspiration: Persepolis rosettes, Persian turquoise and an empire of many peoples.
collections.story: Cyrus the Great founded an empire that stretched from the Aegean to Central Asia, governed through provinces that kept their own languages and customs. The palaces at Persepolis, built by his successors, are bordered with carved rosettes. The Cyrus collection takes a twelve-petal rosette — one petal for each collection — on a deep Persian teal.

emblem.note: Rosette ornament from Achaemenid relief carving; the Faravahar and other religious symbols are deliberately not used.

products.name: Cyrus Lancero
products.summary: A long, slender lancero that puts the wrapper first.
products.description: The lancero’s slim 38 ring gauge gives the wrapper a larger share of the smoke. Pepper, leather and earth define the intended profile.

collections.name: Genghis
collections.inspiration: The steppe, the composite bow and the largest contiguous land empire in history.
collections.story: United under Genghis Khan in 1206, the Mongols built the largest contiguous land empire in history, moving across the steppe with mounted archers whose composite bows were masterpieces of horn, wood and sinew. The Genghis collection is the boldest format of the range — a wide gordo with a drawn bow on bronze.

emblem.note: Material-culture motif; the Soyombo and other national or religious symbols are not used.

products.name: Genghis Gordo
products.summary: A wide 60-ring gordo, the boldest format in the range.
products.description: A sixty-ring gordo for a cool, voluminous draw, with bold spice and dark chocolate at full strength.

collections.name: Charlemagne
collections.inspiration: Carolingian script, manuscripts and the monogram of an emperor.
collections.story: Crowned emperor in Rome on Christmas Day in the year 800, Charlemagne presided over a revival of learning in which scribes developed the clear Carolingian minuscule that shaped later European handwriting. He signed documents with a monogram built from the letters of his name, KAROLVS. The Charlemagne collection uses a monogram of its own on champagne ivory.

emblem.motif: Lozenge monogram inspired by the Karolus signature
emblem.note: Inspired by the structure of Carolingian monograms; it is an original arrangement, not a reproduction of the historical signature.

products.name: Charlemagne Lonsdale
products.summary: A long, elegant lonsdale with a refined character.
products.description: A six-and-a-half-inch lonsdale with a 42 ring gauge: slender, measured and refined, with wood and spice.

collections.name: Saadian
collections.inspiration: Marrakesh, zellige geometry and the emerald and gold of the Saadian court.
collections.story: The Saadians ruled Morocco through the sixteenth and early seventeenth centuries. After victory at the Battle of Alcácer Quibir in 1578, Ahmad al-Mansur built the El Badi palace in Marrakesh, and the dynasty's tombs there remain celebrated for their carved cedar, stucco and zellige — mosaic tilework of interlacing stars cut by hand. The Saadian collection draws an eight-point zellige star in antique gold on deep emerald.

emblem.note: Geometric star from Moroccan zellige tilework, used as ornament; no religious text or flags are used.

products.name: Saadian Robusto
products.summary: A box-pressed robusto, the signature of the Moroccan collection.
products.description: A robusto pressed into a softly squared profile, so it sits flat in the hand and in the box. The Saadian band and box carry the collection’s emerald and zellige identity; the blend is aimed at earth, cedar and warm Moroccan spice.

collections.name: Inca
collections.inspiration: Mountain terraces, stepped stonework and the gold of the Andes.
collections.story: From its capital at Cusco, the Inca state — Tawantinsuyu — joined some four thousand kilometres of the Andes with a road network and terraced the mountains for agriculture. Its masons fitted stone without mortar so precisely that the walls still stand. The Inca collection uses the stepped profile of those terraces in sun gold.

emblem.note: Architectural and textile step motif; sacred imagery such as Inti is deliberately not used.

products.name: Inca Perfecto
products.summary: A perfecto, tapered at both ends.
products.description: A figurado closed at the foot and tapered at the head, one of the most demanding shapes to roll. Spice, cocoa and dried fruit are the intended profile.

collections.name: Imperator
collections.inspiration: The title shared by every empire in the range — the house signature.
collections.story: Imperator began as the Latin acclamation of a victorious commander and became the word from which 'emperor' descends. The Imperator collection is the house's own signature: the crown, laurel and HC monogram of Heritage Cigars, in imperial gold on obsidian.

emblem.note: The master crest of the brand.

products.name: Imperator Salomón
products.summary: The house flagship: a grand salomón.
products.description: The salomón is one of the grandest figurados: a long cigar with a tapered head and a bulb just above a closed, pointed foot. Complex, luxurious and finished with oak, it is the signature of the house.
